paragraph_replacements.1: The decision is whether federation adds useful, authorized service beyond the campus gateway. The proposed 90-day study has two stages: adversarial safety testing, then a confirmatory paired comparison of the gateway baseline $B$ with federation $F$. Campus-local inference and approved frontier access remain descriptive comparators; this two-arm test cannot rank all four options. No pilot or fault-injection study has run. The result here is a testable protocol, not a measured advantage. [C18, C23]
paragraph_replacements.2: First, fix what counts. Sample legitimate demand from authenticated pilot users before either service admits a request, under a prespecified campus, task, and load distribution. One parent-task episode is one requested deliverable, including all calls and retries. Pair episodes under the same frozen task deadline and non-federation entitlements, home-campus rules, local allocation, external approvals, and spending limit. Federation adds only declared remote-campus capacity, including its operating and agreement costs. [C18, C23]
paragraph_replacements.3: Next, define success before looking at outcomes. Set $Y_{si}=1$ only if the deliverable passes task quality, deadline, provenance, version, and approved-handling checks; otherwise set it to zero. Faculty and students must approve executable usefulness and reproducibility rubrics, blinded assessors must judge deliverables, and security staff must check handling separately. Security, legal, procurement, finance, and computing owners must approve processing domains, contracts, controls, measurements, and ceilings. Those approvals and criteria are still missing, so confirmation cannot start. [C18, C23]
paragraph_replacements.4: Keep the offered-demand denominator honest. It includes policy and classification refusals, device mismatch, exhausted budgets, overload, outages, provider rejection, deadline expiry, cancellation after enrollment, and missing adjudication. A refusal may be safe yet still fail useful completion; retries never create new episodes. Exclude malformed or nonresearch traffic only by prespecified outcome-blind rules. Run synthetic malicious probes in the separate safety suite. Admitted-only rates may be reported, but cannot replace offered-demand coverage. [C18]
paragraph_replacements.5: Safety comes before real-data comparison. Begin with public or synthetic work and test stale policy, revocation, malicious tenants, network partitions, campus and provider outages, rejection, ambiguous charges, cancellation, quota contention, crashes, and unsafe fallback. Observe whether policy holds, uncertain charges remain reserved, and recovery avoids duplicate or unauthorized work. An unobserved transition is inconclusive. Forbidden-egress probes are safety tests, not legitimate deliverables in the completion denominator. Real-data pairing requires campus approvals and passed controls. [C23]
paragraph_replacements.6: Then freeze the confirmatory design: configuration, task distribution, cost perspective, and final analysis. Run authorized copies of the same task under comparable load, randomize arm order, blind assessment, isolate caches, and prevent answer leakage. Reset or isolate queues and budgets where replay is valid; never send sensitive work to an unapproved destination to make a pair. Historical gateway logs are not contemporaneous pairs, and duplicate runs count toward the study budget. [C18, C23]
paragraph_replacements.7: Finally, identify independent units. The finite-sample bounds below assume independent, identically sampled paired vectors; the two outcomes within each pair may depend on each other. Shared queues, repeated tasks from one researcher, and common budget depletion defeat naive episode-level independence. Independent reset load blocks with fixed enrollment, or a prespecified cluster or randomized-period analysis, are alternatives. Equal-block weighting changes the target effect unless designed to match task weighting. Calls are not replications; without defensible independent units, inference stays inconclusive. [C18, C23]
paragraph_replacements.15: Plan enrollment against the entire go rule. The accompanying table gives precision and a necessary endpoint condition, not achieved enrollment or joint power. In particular, the economic route's narrow noninferiority margin may drive sample size. Before enrollment, approve a fixed affordable sample, plausible-effect power calculation, and independent-unit design. Expiry of the 90-day window does not lower the evidentiary threshold or authorize extra spending. [C19, C23]
paragraph_replacements.16: Report three distinct outcomes. A demonstrated policy or financial-control failure triggers a safety stop. Adequate simultaneous bounds that exclude the completion floor or both benefit routes support statistical no-go. Bounds certifying neither success nor exclusion, inadequate independent units, incomplete instrumentation, unsettled economics without valid bounds, or underfunded enrollment are inconclusive. Administrative burden and fairness need separate approved criteria and exposure; a favorable pooled completion rate cannot establish them. [C18, C22, C23]
paragraph_replacements.17: The decision therefore rests on incremental benefit under offered-demand accounting, correlated execution, uncertain billing, and independent safety gates. Even a favorable paired result would apply only to the declared tasks, loads, cost perspective, and policy domains. Broader live-service claims require new evidence. Until federation clears those tests and administrative ceilings, this study cannot justify replacing the gateway with separately approved external access. [C18, C21, C23]
